spec_match.rationale: Four live / arrangements read back via currentSrc and naturalWidth — the real source-selection contract — with the correct/broken/wasteful taxonomy matching the HTML update-the-source-set rules.

interactive.rationale: The cases are live DOM whose chosen file and rendered state are re-read on demand via the re-read button; each case pairs markup, rendering, verdict and rationale.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises 'which source the browser chose' plus the mistakes that stop the fallback firing, and the page delivers both, including the wrong-order unreachable-source case.

edge_cases.rationale: This browser is the failure case and the page nails it: untyped source and bare render nothing and are marked bad, the correct arrangement falls through to AVIF, and the prose explains why decode errors cannot trigger fall-through.

conformance.rationale: The one suite assertion covering exactly this page's contract — picture-negotiation-skips-undecodable-types — is syntactically broken (try with no catch/finally) and reports 'Missing catch or finally after try' on the live /conformance/ route, so the page's proven behaviour is unprovable by the suite in every browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: correct case chose image.avif and rendered 960x600 (good); no-type and img-only committed to image.jxl and rendered nothing (bad, as designed); wrong-order chose image.jpg (good); narration counted 2 of 4 rendering; re-read re-ran; only failed requests were the expected undecodable .jxl commits; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Reports log per-case choices and emit showcaseTelemetry.assert('picture-cases-reported', …) with jxlWorks and the good count.

design_system.rationale: Token colours; good/bad lane borders pair with mono verdict text; code blocks and demos on token backgrounds; no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Each case has a heading, its markup as text, a text verdict (not colour alone), images with alt text, and the summary lands in an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; cases stack on mobile with capped image widths.

openQuestions.title: Flag: repair picture-negotiation-skips-undecodable-types (human only)
openQuestions.detail: FOR A HUMAN — the conformance file is immutable to this review and was not touched. The assertion in v155/jpeg-xl-decoding-support-image-jxl-in-blink/conformance.json opens try{ but never closes it with catch/finally, so the runner throws SyntaxError 'Missing catch or finally after try' (verified on the live /conformance/ route) and the assertion fails on every browser forever. The behaviour it encodes is real — this page's 'correct' case demonstrated typed-source fall-through to AVIF on Chromium 141 — so the fix is purely syntactic (append a catch(e){return false;}).

summary: The most valuable page of this feature on a non-decoding browser, and Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) is exactly that: verified over CDP at http://localhost:3000/v155/jpeg-xl-decoding-support-image-jxl-in-blink/picture-fallback/ — the typed fell through to AVIF, the untyped source and bare committed to the .jxl and rendered nothing (marked bad, expected aborted requests), and the wrong-order case exposed the unreachable JXL source. Console otherwise clean, no overflow on either class. The only real defect is in the suite, not the page: the assertion covering this exact contract is syntactically unrunnable and is flagged for a human.
